text: WhatsApp's own message numbers don't add up. On one ordinary day, twenty billion messages sent turned into sixty-four billion, same messages. Where do the extra forty billion come from? The answer is groups. When you fire a message into a group chat, your phone uploads it exactly once. A single copy tagged with a group ID. That's all your battery and your data ever pay for. The multiplying happens on the server. It looks up every member of that group and quietly queues a separate copy for each one. One message in, a hundred messages out. This is server-side fanout, and on the 2nd of April 2014, twenty billion messages people sent fanned out into forty-four billion delivered. Sixty-four billion in a single day. That gap isn't an error, it's fanout made visible. And the real kicker, the cost scales with how big the group is, not with how many people are actually typing. One person can trigger thousands of deliveries, but a few years later, they had to flip fanout completely inside out just to let you read your chats on a laptop. Why? To see it, subscribe
